request: User correction of 2026-11-20 after a pr-followup reply to a reviewer on a PR in a private repository. The PR turned on @typescript-eslint/no-floating-promises for tests and exempted node:test's describe and it. On the removed "off" line the reviewer said the rule was off to keep tests convenient and asked how the PR made the code better. The agent read an objection to the whole rule and posted 85 words of counts and probe results. The user approved: read an inline comment against its line and diff, answer with what already handles the concern, give one deciding fact in a not-applicable reply, extend comment-style's length budget to reviewers with evidence only on request or dispute, cut an over-40-word answer to its answering sentence, record both, and add an eval case.

size.method: wc -w over SKILL.md and each reference at the baseline and at 721d4ae; the comment-style base entry at its recorded private snapshot commit.

growth_reasons: feedback.md anchored-reading paragraph: the user's rule against widening an inline concern; 'any other code the comment names' keeps a correct finding about named code (both reviewers).

feedback.md not-applicable row and anchored paragraph: the user's 'one fact'; 'plus the evidence a request or a dispute from the reviewer calls for' keeps both consistent with comment-style's evidence rule (Claude reviewer, review gate F1).

review.md reply sentence: the user's one-sentence answer and example; 'even by asking whether the change is worth it' resolves the conflict with the worth-it rule seen in a Claude run, and 'neither asks for evidence nor disputes your answer' lets requested evidence follow (review gate F1).

review.md budget paragraph: the user's reader widening, evidence condition, worth-it rule and 40-word check; the check is limited to answers to a question and keeps `Fixed in <commit>.` (both reviewers).

adopted: Both: the 40-word cut used a narrower exception than the evidence rule and applied to every reply, so it could cut a disputed finding or a `Fixed in <commit>.` reply with its allowed sentence; it now covers only an answer to a question, under the same condition, and keeps `Fixed in <commit>.` (fd135b3).
Both: the anchored reading could drop other code the comment names; the claim now includes it (29635b9).
Both: the eval graded neither disposition, a single sentence nor the rule's remaining scope (29635b9).
Both: the comment-style records disagreed and the new entry read as a changelog; the 2026-10-22 entry now states the current rule (fd135b3).
Both: one pr-followup invariant held two decisions and its reason inverted the incident; split and corrected (29635b9).

Claude: the one-fact row blocked evidence the reviewer asks for (29635b9); the eval copied identifiers from the private incident (29635b9); 'the author' remained in the widened section (fd135b3); clauses added to the user's rule are now credited to the invariant they protect; 'should have been' became 'something like'.
declined: Codex M1: the example reply 'skips the tests themselves (describe/it)' is the user's approved example, and its parenthesis and 'still on for any other code' state the exemption's scope.
Codex and Claude: an exception for a comment that names a wider scope in general; a reviewer's 'this PR' would reopen the incident, so only other code the comment names is kept.
review.after_review: Commits 29635b9, fd135b3, b5f3020, 9c08da4 and 721d4ae apply the adopted findings, the eval-driven precedence fix and the review gate's findings; the model pair did not review them again.

evaluation.design: Tool-free dry runs on fake PRs. Executors: T3 delegated tasks on Claude (claude-opus-5-5, effort xhigh) and Codex (gpt-6.2-sol, reasoningEffort xhigh), each told to read only staged copies of the arm's runtime files (both SKILL.md files and their references; no origin.toml, evals or notices) and to use no installed skill; each listed the files it read. The coordinator graded the outputs, not blind. Case A is pr-followup eval 4; round 1 used an earlier prompt with the incident's identifiers, replaced from round 2 on by invented ones. Round 4 ran the whole pr-followup suite. Outputs, arm hashes and grades are in anchored-reply-runs.md.

cases.A: pr-followup eval 4: a reviewer questions something the diff already handles, with tempting probe results available.
cases.B: comment-style regression: B1 a new inline finding with a supplied proof chain and two possible fixes; B2 a reply to a reviewer who disputes the earlier one-sentence answer and asks for a concrete case.
cases.C: pr-followup boundary: an inline comment on a catch block that also names two other handlers outside the diff.
cases.suite: pr-followup evals 1 to 5; eval 4 is case A and eval 5 cuts a long reply after a published fix to `Fixed in <commit>.` and one answering sentence.

expectations.A: pr-followup/evals/evals.json eval 4 (round 1 graded on its first three expectations).
B: B1 starts with the problem, its trigger and SHOP-219, names one fix, carries no proof chain or second fix and no optional label.
B2 gives the concrete case the reviewer asked for.
C: The claim covers the commented catch block and the two named handlers, and nothing wider.
